data.why: The repo's own bundled examples/synthetic_data.json (1,000 participants, full derived-variable schema) is far too large (multi-MB, matching JSON Schema ~65KB with dozens of nested $refs to files outside examples/) to copy under the 200KB budget, so a smaller 40-participant derived-variables cohort and a 10-record linked cancer summary were hand-written to match the same field names, types, units, sentinel values (999/9999 NA codes) and group structure described in the README and examples/DerivedVariables_Schema.json / examples/CancerSummary_Schema.json, including a BMI outlier (46.8), physical-activity outliers (0.0 and 55.0), several missing (null) values, and sentinel NA codes for non-parous participants.

goals: Load the synthetic cohort dataset with its schema and review variable distributions and completeness on the Overview tab
Explore individual variables (e.g. BMI, physical activity) as histograms/bar charts and check summary statistics on the Explore tab
Assess missingness patterns across variables, including sentinel (999/9999) vs true null values, on the Missingness tab
Compare a numeric variable's distribution stratified by a categorical grouping variable (e.g. BMI by menopause status) on the Stratified tab
Build an AND/OR filtered cohort (e.g. premenopausal, parous, BMI>25, current drinker) and inspect the attrition flow diagram on the Cohort Builder tab
Export a Table 1 descriptive statistics summary (optionally stratified) as CSV for the built cohort on the Descriptive tab

review.summary: The tree states the dashboard's purpose and its six-tab workflow (load with dictionary, profile variables, check null vs. not-applicable missingness, compare groups, build an attrition-tracked cohort, export Table 1), and its features are well cut and mostly well evidenced. Before filing it needs the multi-file join either shown working or honestly marked as not shown (the rejection came from the test data, not an app bug), a few screen citations corrected, and some agent-level and button-level actions trimmed.
